FAKE-SYNTHETIC demo visit note: synthetic data, roles only.
Visit notes, Highland Pediatric Center 031 (Texas IDN). The main facility type on the book is Women's Health, and the visit was with the pharmacy director and the women's health clinic manager at the largest site.

I opened with the size of the book: about $766K in net dollars, a few percent of the in-state total (there are many synthetic peers in the state) and a small slice of national dollars. The pharmacy director wanted that context before we talked mix.

The top class is shingles, which leads at a little over two fifths of dollars, far ahead of the national share and with a very high index versus in-state peers. We spent the middle of the visit on that dollar share and on the must-cover ratio: shingles to adult-labelled influenza doses is far above the in-state peer figure. The clinic manager said women's health visits are where most of that shingles volume is scheduled, and they want to keep the current cadence.

On manufacturer mix, GSK Pharm in influenza moved from none of the class doses in the first window to all of them in the second. The pharmacy director had already noticed that influenza share move and asked whether the two-window view would stay in the leave-behind. I said it would.

I asked what is driving purchasing in shingles and which programs are planned for next season. They described a standing women's health counseling script and a planned spring review of the clinic calendar, and they asked for a short peer-index page to take to the next operations meeting.

We did not get to the other must-cover item on today's list. Time ran out after the shingles and influenza discussion, and I did not open the remaining mix point. I will request a shorter follow-up if they can make room next month.

The MSA is live into 2028 and does not renew automatically. A share-floor amendment is on file; we did not discuss terms.
